commits.message:
fix(style)!: resolve style names against the console theme (rich-style-tdn)

`new Console({ theme })` changed nothing. Every style name was resolved when
its renderable or span was built, through the built-in defaults inside
`Style.parse`, before any console could offer a theme, and `Console` stored the
theme it was given without ever reading it. Names now resolve when they
render, in the theme of the console doing the printing, as they do in Rich.

- `Theme.resolve(style)` is the one lookup from a name to a style. It stays
  outside `Style.parse`'s process-wide cache, so two consoles with different
  themes cannot bleed into each other. `Style.parse` parses definitions only.
- `RenderOptions.theme` carries the printing console's theme, and every
  renderable resolves its style names in `render` through one internal
  resolver in `protocol.ts`. Table cells and titles now spread the render
  options instead of building a fresh literal, so the theme reaches them.
- `RichText` keeps its base and span styles as given and resolves them at
  render.
- Template style functions throw a `TypeError` for a fragment whose base style
  is a name: a template runs before any render exists, so the name has no
  theme to resolve against.

Breaking:
- `StyledRenderable.edgeStyle(side)` is now `edgeStyle(side, options)`, and a
  joiner reads edges inside the `render` of the renderable it returns. The
  built-in joiners do.
- `Style.parse` no longer accepts a name: `Style.parse("repr.number")` throws
  `StyleSyntaxError`. Use `Theme.resolve`.
- `RichText.style` is `string | Style`.
- A renderable resolves its style strings at render, so a name its theme lacks
  throws `StyleSyntaxError` when it is printed. Under
  `new Theme(..., { inherit: false })` that includes built-in names such as
  `table.header`, which used to resolve whatever the theme.

docs/style.md, highlighting.md, strip.md and protocol.md describe the new
behaviour, and every changed snippet was compiled and run in a consumer
project.

docs(highlighting): make the custom highlighter examples run (rich-docs-lxn, rich-docs-vaa) (#118)

RequestHighlighter could not run as written. Its patterns used Python's
(?P<name>) group syntax, which a JavaScript RegExp literal rejects. It
set highlights and baseStyle as instance fields, but RegexHighlighter
reads them from the class, so it would have highlighted nothing. It
called the highlighter as a function instead of through .call(). Its
per-group styles also relied on a Console looking http.method up in the
Theme it was given, and no Console does that (rich-style-tdn). The
example now uses static fields and one literal baseStyle, and the page
says which names a baseStyle ending in "." can produce.

RainbowHighlighter passed stylize its arguments as (start, end, style),
but the signature is (style, start, end). It also used Console without
importing it.

The opening example said ReprHighlighter styles file paths, True and a
UUID. It has no path pattern and matches only lowercase true and false,
and the example's "a3f2-..." was styled as a quoted string. The example
and both pattern lists now name only what it styles (rich-docs-vaa).

Both custom highlighter blocks, copied from the page into a TypeScript
project that depends on the package, type-check under strict and
noUncheckedIndexedAccess and print the styles the page describes.
